newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian justice minister resigns in protest.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian justice minister resigns in protest.

text.p: Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Meddein, who advocated death for Palestinians who sell land to Israelis, has resigned, PLO officials said on Monday.
A senior PLO official said Abu Meddein quit to protest the appointment of attorney-general Fayez Abu Rahmeh on Saturday by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat without consulting him.
Abu Meddein could not immediately be reached for comment but his family confirmed he had resigned.

"Freih Abu Meddein resigned on Sunday to protest the appointment by President Arafat of the new attorney-general Fayez Abu Rahmeh without consulting him," a senior PLO official who refused to be identified told Reuters.
The official said Arafat had not yet accepted Abu Meddein's resignation.

Abu Meddein angered Israel in May by announcing the PLO had revived a Jordanian military law banning the sale to Jews of land in the occupied Gaza Strip and West Bank, including East Jerusalem, upon penalty of death.
The law was adopted to prevent Jewish settlement expansion. Settlement building plunged PLO-Israeli peace moves into crisis last March.

Since then, the Palestinian Authority has detained more than 20 suspected land dealers and three more have been found dead. Israel has blamed the Authority for the deaths, but Palestinians denied any involvement.
Israeli officials refused to comment on Abu Meddein's resignation until they received official confirmation.
